summary: First full run on Frameroom (Next.js 15 + Prisma SQLite). Backend: 20 of 22 pytest cases pass, covering auth, lockout, setup returning 403, admin returning 401, client CRUD and validation, gallery create/get/patch/delete, upload validation (non-image, fake MIME type, over 25MB), the public access gate, unlock, thumb/original/zip, changing the password invalidating the unlock cookie, photo delete, random slug returning 404, and settings. Frontend (Playwright): every requested flow works, namely login (including the error), setup and admin redirecting to login, client add/edit/search, create gallery and land in the editor, uploading 3 files with thumbnails at 640px, toasts for the .txt file and the 26MB file, photo delete through the confirm dialog, the copy-link clipboard, turning the password off and on (checked in a logged-out browser), settings (studio name, terracotta preset, logo upload, invalid-hex toast), the public gate (wrong-password error, correct password), hero, grid, lightbox next/prev/arrow keys/Escape/close/download, the download-all zip (3 files), the 404 page, the mobile 390px layout (2 columns, lightbox usable) and logout. Two real bugs found: the login lockout can be bypassed, and PATCH with an invalid clientId returns 500.

critical.issue: The brute-force lockout can be bypassed. clientIp() in src/lib/http.ts uses the FIRST X-Forwarded-For value, and the client controls that value. After 5 failures, sending 'X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4' gives 401 again instead of 429, so an attacker gets unlimited password guesses on the owner login and on gallery passwords. Fix: key the lock on the email alone (or slug alone), or add a second counter per email/gallery; or use the last trusted proxy hop / x-real-ip.

minor.issue: A clientId that does not exist returns 500 (Prisma foreign key constraint violated). POST already validates this. Validate in PATCH too and return 404/400.
No minimum password length on create (the 1-character password 'a' was accepted, 201). PATCH requires at least 4 characters. Make them consistent.
Removing the logo clears logoKey but leaves the old logo file on disk/S3.
For duplicate names, the -N suffix is built from the raw name instead of the sanitized n, so characters that were stripped come back in duplicate filenames.

ui_bugs.issue: toLocaleDateString(undefined, ...) picks up the server's locale. Server-rendered pages show '2026 M11 1' (Dashboard gallery card), while client-rendered pages show 'Nov 1, 2026'. This can also cause a hydration mismatch. Use a fixed locale, e.g. 'en-US'.

integration_issues.issue: SharePanel.copy swallows clipboard errors and always shows the 'Link copied' toast, even when copying fails.

issues: Deleting a photo or gallery uses the browser's native confirm() instead of the app's own styled Modal (no data-testid, does not match the editorial design).
The CSS-columns masonry fills column by column, so the lightbox order (p0, p1, p2 going down each column) does not match the left-to-right order a viewer would expect.
The logo is centred at the top but the form block is left-aligned against the left edge (about 45px). Looks unbalanced at 1920px.
There is no way to delete a client in the UI. The API supports DELETE /api/admin/clients/{id}.

action_items: Fix lockout bypass: don't use client-supplied X-Forwarded-For[0] as the sole lock key. Lock on the email (login) and the gallery id (unlock), whatever the IP.
Validate clientId in PATCH /api/admin/galleries/{id} (it returns 500 today).
Enforce the 4-character minimum password on gallery create (API and UI).
Use a fixed locale in formatDate to avoid the '2026 M11 1' rendering and a hydration mismatch.
Optional: replace native confirm() with the app Modal; add client delete to the UI; only show the copy-success toast when the clipboard write succeeds; delete the old logo file on remove.
critical_code_review_comments: src/lib/http.ts clientIp(): trusting the first X-Forwarded-For entry is the root cause of the lockout bypass.
gallery-access canView: an admin session also unlocks public galleries. Fine for preview, but intended.
The upload route buffers whole files in memory (formData plus arrayBuffer); with multiple 25MB files at once memory use can spike. Acceptable for an MVP.

Security checks that passed: bcrypt $2b$-style via bcryptjs cost 12, fr_session is httpOnly + SameSite=Lax + Secure behind https, the gallery cookie is bound to a password-hash fingerprint (rotating the password invalidates it), passwordHash is never returned, storage keys are protected against path traversal, and sharp metadata rejects files with a fake image MIME type.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested flows functional; 1 medium UI bug

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<url> pytest /app/backend/tests/test_frameroom_api.py. test_lockout_bypass_via_xff and test_patch_invalid_client fail until fixed. Photo/gallery delete uses native confirm(), so in Playwright accept it with page.on('dialog'). Public grid uses CSS columns (columnCount 2 on mobile). Docker deliverables (Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, .env.example, README.md, LICENSE) are present in /app/frontend.
rca of the issue: Lockout bypass: ratelimit identifier = `login:${clientIp}:${email}`, where clientIp = XFF.split(',')[0]. The ingress appends the real IP, but the client-supplied leading value is used, so every request with a new spoofed XFF gets a fresh counter. Reproduce: 5 bad logins for one email, then a 6th with the header 'X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4' returns 401 instead of 429. PATCH 500: db.gallery.update with an unknown clientId throws P2003 and there is no existence check.
